exploit: The caller supplies any absolute URL as `destination`, so the server POSTs the report body to an internal address such as the metadata endpoint.
mitigation: Resolve the destination and require it to be on the allow-listed hosts the contract names.

exploit: The failure response carries the caught message, the resolved destination and the on-disk report path, so a caller learns the storage layout.
mitigation: Return a stable failure code and log the detail server-side.

exploit: The retry loop in step 4 re-POSTs without a ceiling, so one export amplifies into unbounded outbound traffic.
mitigation: Cap the attempts and back off between them.

exploit: Two concurrent exports of the same report interleave in the queue described by step 5 and one overwrites the other's status.
